rules.title: Cartwright Act ban on using or distributing common pricing algorithms as part of an agreement to restrain trade (AB 325)
rules.requirement: Businesses, including landlords and rental companies, may not use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of an agreement to restrain trade. A common pricing algorithm is one with two or more users that uses competitor data to recommend or influence prices or commercial terms.
rules.coverage_conditions: Any business, including apartment rental companies, that uses or distributes a common pricing algorithm (two or more users, uses competitor data to set or influence prices or commercial terms).
rules.exemptions: Single-firm or proprietary algorithms that use only the business's own data are not covered.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only where a common pricing algorithm (two or more users, competitor data) is used or distributed as part of an agreement to restrain trade.

rules.penalty: Criminal fines up to the greater of $6 million or twice the gain or loss for corporations, and the greater of $1 million or twice the gain or loss for individuals; civil fines up to $1 million per violation in AG or district attorney actions; treble damages, injunctive relief and attorney's fees in private suits.
rules.quoted_span: Businesses are expressly prohibited from using or distributing common pricing algorithms as part of an agreement to restrain trade.
rules.conflict_note: General antitrust (Cartwright Act) rule, not specific to rental housing; the source notes apartment rental companies as likely targets. Secondary source; exact subsection split between (a) and (b) not fully specified.

rules.title: Cartwright Act ban on coercing users to adopt common pricing algorithm recommendations (AB 325)
rules.requirement: Businesses may not use or offer a common pricing algorithm if they coerce users to adopt the algorithm's price or other commercial-term recommendations within California for the same or similar products or services.
rules.coverage_conditions: Any business that uses or offers a common pricing algorithm to others, including rental pricing software providers and users.
rules.exemptions: Single-firm or proprietary algorithms that use only the business's own data are not covered.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only where a common pricing algorithm is used or offered and users are coerced to adopt its recommendations.

rules.penalty: Criminal fines up to the greater of $6 million or twice the gain or loss for corporations, and the greater of $1 million or twice the gain or loss for individuals; civil fines up to $1 million per violation in AG or district attorney actions; treble damages, injunctive relief and attorney's fees in private suits.
rules.quoted_span: Separately, businesses are also prohibited from using or offering common pricing algorithms if they coerce users to adopt the algorithm s recommendations on pricing or other commercial terms within California for the same or similar products or services.
rules.conflict_note: General antitrust rule, not specific to rental housing. What constitutes coercion is left to the courts. Secondary source.
